x: The result gives that fillip to Club prestige badly needed at this time and even encourages us to think that next October we may even lead the field with the help of Davies, Hallowell and Newell, to mention names which readily come to mind.

Experience has been given to newcomers to this event, which will help us next April, and now that S.L.H. have lost the great Gordon and we can improve on our team by the inclusion of Davies and Hallowell, it can be hoped that last year's 5th position in the National Relay can be bettered by at least 4 places.
11th Brian Hallowell We have always made a point of allocating the last stage to one of our faster track men and on a number of occasions it has paid dividends.

Davies, Newell and Hallowell led the field after an early dash by Frank Wright. For some unaccountable reason Davies almost stopped with three laps to go and so the race became a duel between Newell and Hallowell.
Brian Hallowell set about the last leg in a very workmanlike manner, much to the consternation of the Woodford runner only a short distance ahead - never have I seen anyone look so worried.

We need some new blood so before April let us see some form from such people as Miller, Thresher, Linstead, Johnston, Stearman, and a return to the team by Hallowell, Davies and Baulch (not new blood but almost indispensable).
